_note: The world's pieces, drawn back to front in the order of `layers`, then in the order listed here. Positions and sizes are logical pixels of the 1440 × 900 design, which the world scales to the window, standing on its bottom. On a phone, a window narrower than `frame.narrow`, the whole design would show the street a quarter of its size under the dock (#229), so the world fits `frame.focus`, the truck with two customers in line, the chalkboard and the employee, across the window and between the top bar's `top` and the dock's `bottom`, standing on the dock. A piece with an `image` (a file path under src/world/art/) shows that image stretched to its size; without one, or when the image fails to load, the world draws a placeholder shape in its `color`, lit as `light` says. An SVG image is drawn once, when it loads, at `artResolution` pixels per logical pixel of its own size. The street's scenery (`backdrop` pieces, #198) is art cut from the design reference, each piece at the reference's place: the five triplexes, with a mirrored copy of the first and copies of the fifth past the design's edges for wide windows; the sidewalk, the curb and the road in tiles one design wide; the sky's gradient stretched, its top colour above the design; under the road, its asphalt below the design, which shows behind the dock and the band on a phone. A backdrop whose image fails to load is a flat shape in its `color`. The truck (#199) is art cut from the same reference, at its place and in its paint order: the body, the espresso machine, the croissant rack, the croissants (the reference's, on three shelves), the counter, the awning and the sign's board, and its shadow on the road, a backdrop under the people's. The counter's image is the strip of the truck in front of the avatar, the counter with the body and the interior behind it, so it hides the avatar's legs and lines up with the truck. The owner, the business name and the lettering stay in code. `shows` keeps a piece to some days: `open` or `closed` ones; those a change to the street from an event card is in effect, `{ "event": <the card's id> }`, except the changes its choices listed in an optional `except` made, such as the move away from the cones; those a product cannot be sold, `{ "unavailable": <the product> }`; or open ones it can be sold, `{ "sells": <the product> }`, such as the steam over the espresso machine. `text` is what a sign or a board says, in French: the road sign, the rival truck, the banner, the « Hors service » card and the truck's lettering each need one, and no other piece takes one. A `lettering` is written in Fredoka in its colour, as tall as its box and centred in it. `fans` sets who fans themselves while it `shows`, as in a heat wave: each customer who comes then holds a fan of `color` with `chance`, which swings `swing` radians each way and back once every `periodMs` real milliseconds. The « MENU » chalkboard (#208) is cut from concept B of the reference (ui_concepts.py), listed with the scenery, before what the events put on the street, such as the road sign, which stands in front of it. `fill` makes the croissants follow the stock: `capacity` units fill the rack, shown in `steps` shelves. The `light.shadowLayer` holds no piece: the world draws the shadows on the ground there, under what stands on it. `spots` are the things in the street the player clicks to open their panel (#208), each a box of the design that opens a dock button, on a tab of « Le camion » if `opens` names one, with a label and its detail in French, over the box or under it with `labelBelow`. A spot shows with its `piece`, or on the days its own `shows` says, or with `staffed` on open days while an employee serves at the truck, whom the street then draws on the sidewalk (in src/world/crowdSettings.ts), or always; a later spot is on top of an earlier one. `streetLegend` is the note that the street can be clicked, in the player's first game for its first `days` days, centred on `x` with its foot at `y`.

light._note: One sun from the upper left, in the morning: every shadow falls to the lower right (#89). Colours mix in 8-bit sRGB, each channel rounding half to even. A top face is its colour mixed with `topFace.light` of `sun`, with a rim mixed with `topFace.rim.light` of `sun`, `topFace.rim.width` deep, along its front edge. A lit side is its colour, a gradient from `litSide.topLight` of `sun` at the top to `litSide.footSlate` of `slate` at the foot. A shade side is its colour mixed with `shadeSide.slate` of `slate`. Cast shadows are `slate` shapes drawn in one layer, blurred by `castShadow.blur` pixels, then shown at `castShadow.opacity`, so overlaps never double; each reaches right by `reach` and down by `drop` of its caster's height. Contact shadows are soft ellipses `contactShadow.depth` as deep as they are wide, at their kind's opacity. Ledges throw `ledgeShadow.opacity` of slate on the wall under them, fading to nothing over their depth in pixels. The city's bricks show their joints at `material.lineOpacity`, in `sun` or `slate`. Over the world only, never over the panels: the painted unevenness (smooth noise, `cells` blotches across) in soft light, the grain (noise `size` pixels square, tiled) in overlay, each around mid-grey by `amplitude` of the full range and seeded by `seed`; the vignette in `vignette.color` (a palette colour), 0 inside `clear` of the radius and `opacity` at the corners; and a warm glow of `sun` from the upper left corner, `opacity` there and gone by `reach` of the diagonal. The simple visual effects drop the unevenness, the grain and the blur.

city._note: The city (#165, #209): the block of the Plateau as `docs/design/reference/city-target.svg` draws it, an island of the grid of `iso2.py` (12 by 12, each square 100 by 50 from 720, 170) floating in the sky, lit by the street's `light` and drawn in its `palette`. Positions and sizes are logical pixels of the `designSize` design. The city shows behind « Ville », which keeps to the window's left (src/ui/TripPanel.css: `frame.panel.left` from its edge, at most `width` wide and at most `share` of the window less `inset`), so the world fits `frame.island`, the island with its tallest roofs, into the room right of the panel: `gap` from it and from the window's right edge, under the top bar's `top` and over the dock's `bottom`, centred there, the sky reaching past the design on every side. In a window narrower than `narrow`, the panel comes down from the top instead, and the whole design is fitted, standing on the window's bottom. A box (the island, the buildings, the truck, the trees, lamps, cones and cars) is `x`, `y`, `width` and `height` on screen; `depth` is how wide its lit wall is across, from its left corner to its front corner, the one nearest the viewer, and its shaded wall takes the rest of `width`; its walls stand `height` − `width` / 2 tall. A box of the grid from `gx`, `gy`, `w` squares along and `d` across, `h` tall, is `depth` 50·w, `width` 50·(w + d), `x` 720 + 50·(gx − gy − d) and its foot 170 + 25·(gx + w + gy + d); src/world/art/cut_city.py prints them. The box is what ranks a piece among the others, what a click finds and what its placeholder fills; `art`, the rectangle of the design its image covers, is where the image is drawn, as cut from the reference with its roof details, awning or stairs. Without `art`, an image is stretched to the box. A piece on a wall (`on`: the box listed before it whose lit wall it is on) is the top of its left edge at `x`, `y`, `width` across and `height` tall, and runs down the wall by half its width, as the wall does; it is drawn with its box, its image at its `art` as drawn, its placeholder along the wall. `backdrop` and `shadows` pieces are flat images (the sky, the clouds, the island with its streets and park, and every cast shadow of the reference in one image, so they never darken twice), drawn in the order listed; `scenery` is a tree, a lamp, a cone or a car, which ranks among the buildings and opens nothing. In the layers under `light.shadowLayer`, the pieces are drawn in the order listed; in those over it, the boxes are drawn from the farthest to the nearest, the people walking among them. `shows` keeps a piece to some times: `truckOpen` or `truckClosed`, the minute the truck serves or not, on a closed day or while the owner is away with nobody at the truck; `bakeryRuns` or `bakeryForRent`, the days the bakery runs, through its notice, or not; `{ "contract": <grocer> }` while that grocer's contract runs. `opens` is what a click on it opens: `{ "trip": <place> }` « Aller à… », `fournil` the « Fournil » of « Gérer le camion », `contracts` the « Contrats » screen; nothing opens a trip in a Défi. While the pointer is on a box that opens something, its name shows over it in a `label`, `above` its top: its place's name, its grocer's, or the bakery's sign while it is for rent. `place` is the place in town it is, one building each, and `grocer` the grocer whose shop it is, one each: the reference has no grocers, so their three shops are iso2.py's café in empty lots, each awning in its grocer's colour. A sign's `text` is its words, in its `trim` colour on its `color`. `routes` are each place's way from `truck.counter` to its door, along the sidewalks and over the crosswalks: the Caisse's follows the reference's dashed way, then goes to the bank's door. `deliveries` is the van's way out from where it starts (`from`: the bakery when it runs, or else the truck) and back, along the avenue's south lane east of the truck, its stop at each grocer, when it drives as shares of the day replayed, and its size, as the reference's cars; `truck.window` where the owner, then each employee at the truck, stands to serve in the hatch, their feet under it; `truck.line` where the line stands, as the reference's three customers, `max` at most, each customer for `minutes` of the day after they came; `bakers` where the bakers stand while the bakery runs, and `deliveries.deliverers` where the deliverers stand by the van parked, each one a `step` after the one before. `figure.scale` is how big the street's people are drawn in the city, the reference's, and `seed` picks the looks of those in line. `path` is the dashes of the day's trip, with a `dot` at its door and a `ring` under the owner walking, and `label` the « En route vers… » over its door, `rise` above it. The `light.shadowLayer` holds no piece.
